mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines an opaque material?

options.A: It allows all light to pass through it
options.B: It allows some light to pass through it
options.C: It does not allow any light to pass through it
options.D: It changes colour when light passes through it

mcqs.answer: It does not allow any light to pass through it
mcqs.explanation: An opaque material blocks the transmission of light, so no light passes through it. Option A describes a transparent material, B describes a translucent material, and D is unrelated to opacity.

mcqs.learning_point: Amount of light passing through different materials
mcqs.question: If a beam of light passes through a transparent material, then a translucent material, then an opaque material, in which order does the amount of light transmitted decrease?
mcqs.explanation: Transparent materials let most light through, translucent materials let only part of the light through, and opaque materials let none. Therefore the light intensity decreases in the order Transparent > Translucent > Opaque.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday use of a transparent material?
mcqs.explanation: Glass windows are transparent, allowing us to see outside while keeping weather out. The other options are made of opaque materials and do not serve a transparency function.

mcqs.question: A student wants to read the label inside a bottle without opening it. Which material should the bottle be made of?
mcqs.explanation: Transparent glass lets light pass through without scattering, so the label inside can be seen clearly. Opaque materials block the view, and translucent paper would blur the label.

mcqs.question: Which statement is true about translucent materials?

options.A: They allow all light to pass through clearly
options.B: They allow no light to pass through
options.C: They allow some light to pass but objects cannot be seen clearly
options.D: They completely change the colour of the light

mcqs.answer: They allow some light to pass but objects cannot be seen clearly
mcqs.explanation: Translucent materials let part of the light through, but the light is scattered, so objects on the other side appear blurry. Option A describes transparent, B describes opaque, and D is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Why can't you see objects on the other side of an opaque wall?

options.B: The wall absorbs or blocks all light
options.C: The wall bends light around it
options.D: The wall lets light pass but scatters it

mcqs.answer: The wall absorbs or blocks all light
mcqs.explanation: An opaque wall prevents light from passing through by absorbing or reflecting it, so no image can be formed on the other side. It does not merely reflect all light (A) nor bend it (C), and scattering implies some transmission, which does not occur in opaque materials.

mcqs.learning_point: Amount of light passing through different materials
mcqs.question: Arrange the following materials from most light transmitted to least: clear glass, frosted glass, thick wooden board.

options.A: Clear glass > Frosted glass > Thick wooden board
options.B: Thick wooden board > Frosted glass > Clear glass
options.C: Frosted glass > Clear glass > Thick wooden board
options.D: Clear glass > Thick wooden board > Frosted glass

mcqs.answer: Clear glass > Frosted glass > Thick wooden board
mcqs.explanation: Clear glass is highly transparent, allowing the most light. Frosted glass is translucent, allowing less light. A thick wooden board is opaque, allowing virtually no light. Hence the order is Clear glass > Frosted glass > Thick wooden board.

mcqs.question: In designing a classroom, which transparent material is most suitable for the ceiling to allow natural daylight while minimizing heat gain?
mcqs.explanation: Frosted acrylic diffuses daylight, providing illumination without the glare and excessive heat that clear glass would transmit. Opaque metal and thick wood block light entirely, while clear glass lets in too much heat. Therefore frosted acrylic is the best choice for a daylighting ceiling.
